cards.text: New king in Judah, friend. Ahaz son of Jotham takes the throne at twenty years old and reigns in Jerusalem sixteen years, while Pekah son of Remaliah, king of Israel, is in his seventeenth year. And unlike David his father, the great king he descends from, Ahaz does not do what was right in the eyes of the LORD his God.

cards.question: King Ahaz doesn't do what was right in the eyes of the LORD. Whose ways does he walk in instead?

cards.text: And then it gets darker. Ahaz even sacrifices his son in the fire, following the abominations of the nations the LORD had driven out before the Israelites.

cards.question: King Ahaz sacrifices and burns incense only at the temple in Jerusalem.

cards.text: Then Rezin, king of Aram, and Pekah, king of Israel, come up to wage war against Jerusalem. They besiege Ahaz but can't overcome him.
At that time Rezin recovers Elath for Aram and drives out the men of Judah. He sends the Edomites into Elath, and they're still living there when this was written.

cards.question: Jerusalem holds, but Judah has lost Elath to Aram. Who does King Ahaz send messengers to for help?
King Ahaz wants the king of Assyria to save him. In his message, what does Ahaz call himself?

cards.text: Servant AND son? Friend, that's not a message, that's adoption paperwork, and Ahaz doesn't send it empty-handed.

cards.question: Ahaz sends a gift to the king of Assyria along with his message. What is it?

answers.text: Silver and gold from the LORD's house and the palace
Horses and chariots from the royal stables
Bronze and iron from the city armories

cards.text: Ahaz hits send, and Assyria actually writes BACK. The king of Assyria responds and marches up to Damascus, the capital of Aram (Isaiah 7:8).

cards.question: The king of Assyria captures Damascus and puts Rezin to death.
The king of Assyria leaves the people of Damascus in their city.

cards.text: Then King Ahaz goes to Damascus to meet Tiglath-pileser, king of Assyria, sees the altar there and sends Uriah the priest a model of it and complete plans for building it. That's somebody on vacation texting their contractor a photo and the measurements before they've even flown home.

cards.question: King Ahaz sends Uriah the priest a model of the Damascus altar and complete plans for it. What does Uriah do?

answers.text: Builds the altar by Ahaz's instructions
Sends the plans back to Damascus
Locks the plans away in the temple

cards.question: Uriah the priest finishes building the altar before King Ahaz gets back from Damascus.
King Ahaz comes back from Damascus and sees the new altar Uriah the priest built. What does Ahaz do?

answers.text: Approaches it and presents offerings on it
Has it torn down and carried away
Orders Uriah to move it outside the city

cards.text: He offers his burnt offering and his grain offering, pours out his drink offering and splatters the blood of his peace offerings on the new altar. That's not a test run, friend, that's a GRAND OPENING with the ribbon AND the big scissors.

cards.question: The bronze altar that stood before the LORD sits between the new altar and the house of the LORD. What does King Ahaz do with the bronze altar?

answers.text: Moves it to the north side of the new altar
Sends it off to the king of Assyria
Breaks it apart and melts down the bronze

cards.text: Then King Ahaz gives Uriah the priest his orders. He says he'll use the bronze altar himself, to seek guidance.

cards.question: King Ahaz says he'll use the bronze altar to seek guidance. Which altar does he order to get the morning burnt offering, the evening grain offering and all the people's offerings?

answers.text: The altars on the high places

cards.text: Friend, that new altar just got put on EVERY shift, morning AND evening, no days off. And Ahaz orders all the blood of the burnt offerings and sacrifices splattered on it too.

cards.question: Uriah the priest pushes back on King Ahaz's commands about the altars.
King Ahaz cuts off the frames of the movable stands in the temple and removes the bronze basin from each one.

cards.text: He also takes down the Sea from the bronze oxen that were under it and puts it on a stone base. This man is pulling things off and moving things around like he's got his own home makeover show.
Then he removes the Sabbath canopy they had built in the temple and closes the royal entryway outside the house of the LORD. The KING'S entryway, and the king himself closes it.

cards.question: King Ahaz removes the Sabbath canopy and closes the royal entryway on account of the king of ___.

cards.text: The rest of Ahaz's acts are written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah, so if you want the extended cut, that's where it lives. Then Ahaz rests with his fathers and is buried with them in the City of David.

cards.question: After Ahaz is buried in the City of David, which son of his reigns in his place?
